elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2.2: "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" — the $60 million Development Cost gate and the pre-first-Regulatory-Approval window in the original have been deleted, so the election is unconditional. There are no Order Forms in this co-development structure, so the Order Form limb is inapplicable. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returned false, but on inspection of the operative text the right is expressly present and unconditional, so the mechanical miss is a regex artefact, not a substantive gap.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" replaces the redacted [***] notice period; 30 days is at (not above) the preferred ceiling and the notice is expressly written.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "and SFJ will refund to PB, pro rata, any amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of such termination" — the refund is expressly pro rata (not merely post-termination-period), runs from Vendor (SFJ) to Customer (PB), and is triggered by the 14.2.2 convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Added operative sentence: "No Termination for Convenience by SFJ. SFJ shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term." "Term" is a defined term (1.1.185 / Section 14.1), so the anchor is not undefined. Retained SFJ exits at 14.2.6 (Change of Control of PB) and 14.2.10 (JSC deadlock after Executive Officer escalation) are event-triggered, so they do not contradict the new prohibition, though 14.2.6's "sole discretion ... at any time following a Change of Control" leaves a broad post-trigger discretion worth monitoring.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered notice is "thirty (30) days", which is outside the literal 60–90 day fallback band (it is more Customer-favourable, but the fallback element as written is not satisfied).

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: 14.2.2 retains "an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination", plus continuing Approval Payment exposure. No three-months-of-fees cap appears anywhere in the rendered text; the cap is only offered in the margin comment, which is not operative.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The added sentence bars SFJ convenience termination outright during the Term, which a fortiori satisfies an end-of-term-only limitation; no SFJ convenience right survives to be exercised mid-term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no SFJ convenience termination right exists after the added prohibition, so no notice period is required for one. The condition does not apply.

reasons: Preferred level is complete in operative language: unconditional PB convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts, and an express bar on SFJ convenience termination during the Term. The redline is therefore position-complete at the preferred level; the fallback shortfalls (30 vs 60–90 days, no three-months fee cap) do not matter because only one level need be met.

Deterministic 'Customer convenience termination present: false' is a false negative on substance — the rendered 14.2.2 contains an express, ungated 'PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice'. Verify the regex pattern rather than the drafting.

Minimality holds: the only deletions are the two gates that blocked the right (the $60 million Development Cost threshold and the pre-first-Regulatory-Approval window) and the redacted notice period; the 300% Development Cost payment, the Trial Data Package purchase mechanic, the Approval Payment continuation, the Section 6.2 adjustment and the Section 6.7 Buy-Out credit are all retained verbatim. The Vendor prohibition is a concise insertion for element 4 with no survival tail, expense language or extra procedure.

Intent preserved: SFJ's event-triggered exits (14.2.6 Change of Control, 14.2.10 JSC deadlock) and their payment formulas survive without contradiction, and no cross-reference is left dangling (Sections 11.1.1.4, 6.2, 6.7 and ARTICLE 6 references are untouched).

Commercial watch-item, not a checklist defect: because the pre-Regulatory-Approval window was removed, the retained 300% Development Cost payment now attaches to a convenience termination exercised at any point in the Term, including post-approval. That is a heavy exit price on an otherwise at-will right; if the counterparty accepts the 30-day right, consider a follow-on ask to cap or taper the 300% payment (the three-months-of-fees cap sits only at the fallback, so it is correctly excluded from this preferred-level edit and correctly offered in the comment).

If the counterparty pushes back and the fallback is taken up, all four fallback elements must be rendered in operative text — notice moved into the 60–90 day band and an express cap replacing the 300% formula — since the margin offer alone will not make the fallback level complete.
